, said the company’s strategy remains centered on strengthening its subscription business, expanding advertising and improving efficiency, with recent operating results providing what she described as evidence that the approach is working.

Speaking at Goldman Sachs’ Communacopia + Technology Conference, Witz said Sirius XM reported solid subscription performance in the second quarter, including higher average revenue per user, low churn and strong customer satisfaction. Advertising revenue rose 5% in the quarter, while the company remains on track to deliver $100 million in gross cost savings this year, she said.

children: Witz reiterated the company’s free-cash-flow expectations of $1.375 billion this year and $1.5 billion next year, compared with $1.25 billion last year. She said lower capital expenditures for the satellite fleet as that investment cycle is completed next year should support cash generation and create greater capacity for shareholder returns, including share repurchases.
Subscription initiatives target retention and demand

Witz said Sirius XM’s in-car business remains a significant competitive advantage, despite perceptions that satellite radio could face a rapid decline. The company is seeking to expand vehicle penetration at appropriate economics, increase used-car penetration and attract customers through extended-duration plans, she said.

children: The company is also emphasizing a more personalized in-car experience through SiriusXM with 360L. The platform is used by roughly 20% of self-pay subscribers and is expected to be available in just over 60% of new-car sales by year-end, according to Witz.

Data from the platform is helping Sirius XM make content and product decisions, including the addition of local sports content, she said. Witz added that 360L has produced better conversion, retention and ARPU, while providing flexibility to offer different packages and enhanced features.

Second-quarter churn was 1.4%, Witz said. While the company expects modestly greater self-pay net-add losses this year than last year, she attributed part of that outlook to a reduced reliance on unpublished discounts and a shift toward customers rolling from trials into full-price plans. She said the transition may pressure near-term net additions but should improve the longer-term revenue profile.

Sirius XM is also using its Companion offering and continuous-service initiative to support retention. The Companion plan allows a paying subscriber to provide another household member with a radio or streaming subscription at zero ARPU. Witz said Sirius XM has about 300,000 Companion additions and that more than 80% of users say the feature has added value to their subscription.

Continuous service is designed to reduce friction when customers change vehicles by preserving their subscription, profile, preferences and streaming credentials while they determine where to place the service. Witz said future auto-transfer capabilities could further reduce customer leakage.
Lower-priced packages and exclusive content

Witz said Sirius XM is pursuing lower-priced, content-focused packages to broaden its addressable market while continuing to add value to its broader subscription bundle. The company has launched its ad-supported Play music offering at $7 per month and is introducing Sports Pass at $5 per month.

Sports Pass will include Sirius XM’s sports programming, including play-by-play rights across the four major leagues, other sports coverage, sports talk and local sports stations through Audacy. Witz said the product could attract listeners who already subscribe to a music service but want broader sports access.

The company also sees opportunities in comedy and true crime. Witz cited recent additions including Sebastian Maniscalco and said Sirius XM is launching an ABC 20/20 channel after seeing success with its Dateline channel.

Witz described human curation, exclusive programming and live content as the company’s key differentiators. She pointed to country channel The Highway, which she said reaches 25% of Sirius XM subscribers each month, as an example of the company’s “fandom” strategy built around artist discovery, personalities, listener participation and exclusive events.
Advertising partnerships and spectrum optionality

On advertising, Witz said Pandora accounts for about half of Sirius XM’s advertising revenue. The company is expanding its third-party representation business through partnerships involving SoundCloud, Amazon’s DSP, Apple’s podcast ecosystem and YouTube.

With YouTube, Sirius XM expects to reach 255 million monthly listeners, representing 90% of the U.S. population above age 13, Witz said. The partnership is beginning to launch and is expected to make a small contribution this year, with a more meaningful impact anticipated in the second half of next year. The company will monitor advertiser demand, repeat business and revenue as it evaluates the deal’s progress.

Witz also discussed the company’s spectrum portfolio, including 25 MHz of S-band spectrum used for its service and 5 MHz on either side in WCS blocks acquired in 2024. She said Sirius XM has seen interest related to potential spectrum uses, including direct-to-device applications, but is prioritizing value over speed.

Potential structures could include a sale, lease, joint venture or other commercialization arrangement, Witz said, adding that the company must consider technical and regulatory feasibility. She said the company has reached its target leverage ratio and intends to prioritize investment in the business, maintain leverage and return excess capital to shareholders.
About Sirius XM

Sirius XM Holdings Inc provides subscription-based audio entertainment and information services in the United States and Canada. Its SiriusXM service delivers commercial-free music, sports, news, talk and entertainment programming through satellite radio and internet streaming, including its mobile app and connected-vehicle platforms.

The company offers a broad range of exclusive and licensed content, including live sports coverage, original talk and comedy programs, news services, podcasts, and music channels organized by genre and artist.
